name: ISTEXT
description: ISTEXT returns TRUE if the supplied value is text, and FALSE otherwise.
tldr: Tests whether a value is text.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value, cell reference, or formula result to test.

basicExample.description: Check a cell containing a word
basicExample.explanation: "Hello" is a text string, so the function returns TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: An empty string is text
advancedExamples.scenario: A formula returns "" to indicate no data.
advancedExamples.explanation: A1 holds a formula returning ""; because that is text, ISTEXT returns TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: Numbers are not text
advancedExamples.explanation: 42 is a number, not text, so the result is FALSE.

howItWorks: ISTEXT checks the data type of the supplied value. If it is a text string—including numbers stored as text and the empty string ""—it returns TRUE; numbers, logicals, errors, blank cells, and dates return FALSE.

howToSteps.name: Pick the value
howToSteps.text: Select the cell or value to test.

howToSteps.name: Read the result
howToSteps.text: TRUE means text, FALSE means not.

limitations: Numbers formatted as text return TRUE.
An empty string "" produced by a formula is considered text.
Errors, logicals, and numbers return FALSE.

commonErrors.cause: A number is stored as text.
commonErrors.fix: Convert it to a number with VALUE() or Text to Columns.
Use ISNUMBER to test for dates.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ISTEXT works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: Does ISTEXT catch numbers stored as text?
faq.answer: Yes, a numeric value stored as text returns TRUE.

faq.question: What about blank cells?
faq.answer: A truly blank cell returns FALSE; only an actual empty string or text returns TRUE.

faq.question: Is "" considered text?
faq.answer: Yes, the empty string is text, so ISTEXT returns TRUE for it.
